summary.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 6% YoY to Rs 269 crore, but EBITDA fell 27% to Rs 45 crore (16.8% margin) and PAT dropped to Rs 0.7 crore after a PCMC WtE disruption.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 6% YoY to Rs 269 crore on higher project volumes and tariff escalation, while EBITDA margin compressed to 16.8% from 24.4% a year ago, driven by vehicle hiring and transport costs, a 18% YoY rise in employee costs (34% of revenue), and about Rs 10 crore of deferred waste disposal costs from CIDCO bio-mining closure. PAT was Rs 0.7 crore after a Rs 7 crore prepayment charge on the Antony Lara refinancing, which cut the term loan rate from 10.25% to 8.25%. A July 8 landslide/legacy waste mound collapse at the PCMC WtE site killed nine people and halted WtE operations, with restart guided for early October and an estimated Rs 22-24 crore impairment (before insurance) flagged as exceptional. Management called the quarter's profitability transitional, but gave no revised FY27 margin guidance.

segments.name: Collection & Transportation (C&T)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 156 crore, +10% YoY; about 0.55 million tons handled, +6% YoY. Share of revenue 62% vs 60% a year ago. Margin pressured by repairs and maintenance and ageing contracts; management does not disclose segment margins.

segments.name: MSW Processing
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 75 crore, +3% YoY; about 0.85 million tons, +5% YoY. Growth slowed as CIDCO bio-mining contract ended; RDF sales about 40,000 tons, down about 28% YoY, which management calls timing-related. Net RDF realisation put at upwards of Rs 300/ton vs about Rs 250 a year ago.

segments.name: Waste-to-Energy (PCMC, Antony Lara)
segments.commentary: Generated over 20 million units in Q1 before suspension after July 8 incident. Tipping fee income continues; power sales are hit during the shutdown. Fixed costs of about Rs 2.5-3 crore per month (about Rs 7 crore total) hit P&L until restart in early October; impairment estimate Rs 22-24 crore before insurance.

segments.name: Construction & Demolition recycling
segments.commentary: Running close to 600-650 tons per day against 600 tpd capacity (+/-10%), after BMC policy made large builders send C&D waste to processing. Recovery rate stated at 96%.

segments.name: Compost and RDF
segments.commentary: Compost sales about 6,000 tons, broadly stable. RDF sales down about 28% YoY (see processing).

guidance_outlook: WtE PCMC restart expected by first week / second week of October 2026 after OEM and Hitachi certification; full revenue from that point.
Material recovery and composting restarted July 28 at about 400 tons per day.
Management expects margins to improve slightly from Q2 onwards but not as weak as Q1; respite from transport re-negotiation and labour escalation expected in H2 FY27.

Labour cost ratio expected to normalise from 34% toward the historical 30-31% range over the next three quarters, supporting margin expansion in FY28; long-term EBITDA margin in the 22-24% range cited by an analyst, with management saying the internal threshold is a return to historical margin trend.

New GNIDA road sweeping contract (Rs 243 crore over 5 years, plus 2-year extension) to start Q3 FY27, about Rs 46 crore first-year revenue. BMC contract adds about 1,500 tons per day and Atkoli project 600-800 tons per day, reaching full run-rate by Q4 FY27.
Growth guidance: existing portfolio 6-9%, new business 10-15%, with lumpy recognition of 2-3 quarters after LOA.
Target portfolio mix moving from about 70:30 (C&T:processing) toward 50:50, with processing and WtE the margin-accretive focus.
capex_capacity: Andhra Pradesh WtE projects at Kadapa and Kurnool: land possessed at both sites; EPC/technology partner JFE India completed civil designs; civil contractor mobilised at Kadapa, Kurnool expected within weeks; financial closure at final stage. Incremental debt started for AP WtE.
Atkoli processing project (Thane) to be running by Q4 FY27, with capex reimbursement expected in Q4 and higher margin profile.

Management is evaluating compressed biogas (CBG) as part of integrated waste projects (city sends about 1,000 tons; dry fraction to WtE, wet to CBG) and is still evaluating auto scrap diversification.
Gross borrowings up about Rs 22 crore vs Q4 FY26, attributed to AP WtE and new C&T (BMC) contract working capital.
Debt maturity: about Rs 40 crore due within 12 months; about Rs 350 crore due over 3-5 years (per management's split of Rs 435 crore).
demand_pricing: Bio-mining (CIDCO) contract completed; final-phase inert disposal costs of about Rs 10 crore hit Q1 and are not expected to recur.
C&T tipping fees range about Rs 1,800-4,200/ton depending on scope, vehicles and contract duration; some contracts (Thane, Jhansi, Varanasi) bill per household, unit or trip rather than tonnage.

Cost pressures cited: fuel volatility, repairs and maintenance, additives, fabrication and cutting gases (spiked after Gulf conflict), and a Maharashtra DA revision. Escalation clauses cover about 80% of operating cost, with a lag of about 6 months.
Mandatory C&D waste routing by BMC has lifted tonnages after an initial shortfall.
Management cites a Bombay High Court monitoring committee supportive of Kanjurmarg operations; Supreme Court matter listed 12 August 2026.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the WtE operation and the near-term revenue impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Material recovery and composting restarted July 28. WtE is expected back by early October, with fixed costs of Rs 2.5-3 crore per month (about Rs 7 crore total) and power sales hit while tipping fees continue.

qa_highlights.question: Why did processing revenue growth moderate and what is the margin outlook into Q2-Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: CIDCO bio-mining ended last quarter, so processing volumes softened. Margin pressure from transport and hiring should ease somewhat, with Atkoli back by Q4 and transport re-negotiation; labour escalation relief expected in H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is a sub-20% EBITDA margin possible in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Processing is not seeing much pressure, but C&T faces repairs and ageing-contract pressure. FY27 has upticks from the BMC contract from Q3 and Atkoli capex reimbursement in Q4; management aims to return to historical margins, with quarter-to-quarter variation.

qa_highlights.question: How much is the refinancing and the receivable from the Corporation?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 140 crore of Lara Renewables debt was refinanced with tenure extended to 15 years and net benefit of Rs 14 crore after Rs 6 crore prepayment charge. The Rs 15 crore court-favoured receivable is still pending with the Corporation.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Rs 10 crore incremental transport cost is recurring?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was a cumulative closure cost of the CIDCO bio-mining contract, not repeated, and no similar cost is expected in the coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the RDF sales decline and realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: RDF sales fell 28% YoY because of timing, with new customers being added and sales from PCMC plant alongside CIDCO and Kanjurmarg. Net realisation is above Rs 300/ton vs about Rs 250 last year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee costs spike and will it be recovered?
qa_highlights.answer: Labour Code changes restated actuarial assumptions and new headcount added costs. Most is recoverable via tender escalation with about a 6-month lag; labour cost ratio is expected to normalise to 30-31% and margins to recover in FY28.

risks_watch: WtE PCMC restart timing: guided for first/second week of October 2026 after OEM and Hitachi certification; fixed costs of Rs 2.5-3 crore per month (about Rs 7 crore) until restart, plus power sales loss.

Impairment of Rs 22-24 crore (before insurance recovery) on PCMC WtE damage; management says the estimate is still evolving and more detail will come in Q2 results; auditors have flagged the item pending OEM review.
Labour cost ratio at 34% of revenue vs 30-31% historically; escalation recovery lags about 6 months and management frames the normalisation as taking the next three quarters.
Cost pressures from fuel, repairs and maintenance, additives, cutting gases and the Maharashtra DA revision; transport re-negotiation outcome is pending and relief is guided for H2 FY27.
Q4 FY27 is the test of run-rate volumes: BMC (about 1,500 tpd) and Atkoli (600-800 tpd) ramp in Q3-Q4; management says the contract-based revenue recognition lags LOAs by 2-3 quarters.

Supreme Court hearing on the Kanjurmarg matter listed 12 August 2026; the Rs 15 crore receivable from the Corporation is still pending; Andhra WtE projects (Kadapa, Kurnool) need financial closure and incremental debt, with gross borrowings up about Rs 22 crore QoQ.
